intro: Many people help keep us well. Doctors check our bodies. Nurses give shots and answer questions. Dentists care for our teeth. Pharmacists get medicine ready.
Our feelings are part of our health too. In this unit you will learn what happens at a checkup. You will learn to name feelings and find ways to feel calm. You will learn who to ask for help.
bigQuestion: Who helps us stay well, and how can we help ourselves?

timeline.t: You check in at the doctor's office with a grown-up.
A nurse measures how tall you are.
You step on a scale to see your weight.
The doctor listens to your heart with a stethoscope.
The doctor looks in your ears with a small light.
You may get a shot that helps your body fight germs.
If you feel nervous, you take slow, calm breaths.
You ask your questions and say thank you.

words.d: a person who studied a long time to help keep bodies well
a helper who cares for sick people and checks how they are
a visit to the doctor to make sure you are well
a tool doctors use to listen to your heart and lungs
a shot or medicine that helps your body learn to fight a germ
a time when someone needs help right away
what is going on inside you, like happy, sad or mad
breathing in and out slowly to help your body relax

test.q: Who gets medicine ready at a drugstore?
test.why: A pharmacist gets medicine ready and explains how to use it.

test.q: What does a doctor use to hear your heart?
test.why: A stethoscope lets the doctor hear your heart.

test.q: What does a vaccine help your body do?
test.why: A vaccine helps your body learn to fight a germ.

test.q: What number do you call in an emergency?
test.why: 911 is the number for fast help.
Only take medicine from a trusted adult.

choices: A visit to make sure you are well
test.why: A checkup is a visit when you are not sick.

test.q: Which one is a body clue for worry?
test.why: A tight tummy is a body clue for worry.

test.q: How do you do calm breathing?
test.why: Calm breathing is slow breathing in and out.

test.q: Is it okay to feel nervous at the doctor?
choices: Yes, and you can ask questions
test.why: Feeling nervous is okay, and doctors like questions.

test.q: Who is a school helper for feelings?
test.why: A school counselor listens and helps kids with feelings.

write.prompt: Pretend a friend is nervous about a checkup. What would you tell your friend? Use two facts from this unit to help your friend feel brave.
tips: Name one helper and what they do.
Name one tool, like a stethoscope.
Share one way to feel calm.
